Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum with procurement: 

Summary from our call:
- ACME will evaluate Redwood for user-facing summarization and search in a regulated product line.
- Key blocker: ACME requires either 0-retention for any PII-containing requests, or a contractually guaranteed short log retention window (<=7 days) and strict KMS separation.
- They want evidence of logging controls, and a DPA amendment to reflect the exception.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rafael to share a short architecture note that shows how we can support 0-retention or a 7-day shortened logs flow (including KMS and audit logs).
2) Legal (David) to propose DPA language/redlines for the exception and DocuSign route.
3) Marissa to confirm any pricing/commitment changes required for the exception.
4) Emily / ACME to share the security questionnaire and any mandatory procurement SLAs.

Attachments: please reply with the questionnaire when you have a moment — I attached the short mutual action plan template for scheduling.

Thanks — we think this is doable but want to be explicit on tradeoffs and timeline.

Best,

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps — data retention exception request

Hi Emily — thanks, attached is a short technical note and options matrix. High level:

Options we can support:
1) 0-retention (preferred for ACME's high-risk flows):
   - Ingest and process requests in-memory where possible, do not persist request/response bodies to disk or long-term logs.
   - Short-lived ephemeral KVs in the runtime; KV cache eviction is immediate post-response.
   - Audit logs still exist for operational metrics but can be reduced to metadata-only (timestamp, request_id, model_version) with no content.
2) 7-day shortened logs:
   - Store request/response payloads encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys.
   - Automatic deletion job runs daily to purge content after 7 days.
   - Access restricted to a small ops group; access audited via SIEM.

Tradeoffs:
- 0-retention: best for privacy but may limit debugging and quality investigations. We can provide a redacted sampling flow for root-cause analysis.
- 7-day storage: easier for debugging but requires KMS integration and DPA language to guarantee deletion.

Timeline (proposed):
- Technical note + config snippet: by Mon 23 Nov
- DPA redlines for legal review: by Tue 24 Nov
- Procurement / DocuSign flow: target sign-off by Fri 27 Nov if legal review is quick.

Attachments: proposed_dpa_redlines.docx, architecture_note_0ret_vs_7day.pdf

Let me know if you want a short call to walk through the architecture. Happy to set up an SE-led demo of the 0-retention mode.

Cheers,
Rafael
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com

Hi Emily / Procurement —

Quick pricing note from our side: supporting a strict 0-retention flow for a customer-managed KMS and additional engineering controls may require a small platform configuration fee and a minimum committed capacity for the first 12 months (recommended for operational predictability). I can provide a formal term sheet but here are the high level options:

- Option A (0-retention): one-time config fee $10k + monthly reserved throughput commit.
- Option B (7-day retention): no one-time fee, minor monthly surcharge (approx. +5%) to cover KMS and deletion job costs.

If ACME is OK sharing expected volume ranges, I can give exact numbers. Either way, we will reflect the retention exception in the DPA as a schedule or amendment.

Best,

Emily / ACME legal — thanks for the questionnaire. We reviewed Rafael's note and prepared a short set of DPA redlines that capture the 0-retention and 7-day options. High level legal position:

- We can agree to a contractual 0-retention obligation for specified endpoints/flows with an explicit exclusion for operational debugging tied to redacted sampling.
- For the 7-day option, we will bind deletion schedules to a cron job and provide audit evidence on request.
- We'll need ACME to sign a mutual exhibit that identifies the flows subject to the exception (to avoid a global 0-retention requirement).

I uploaded the redlines to DocuSign and included the link below; Rafael's doc also has marked language. If that looks good to ACME legal, we can start signatures and then trigger the configuration work.
